name: Different Kinds of Orgasm — Overview
summary: Orgasms are not a single on/off event—intensity and sensation vary by stimulation type and timing. Treating climax as a checkbox limits discovery; exploring G-region, deep cervical, and dual (simultaneous internal + external) orgasms can unlock richer, more intense experiences than one default approach every session.
detailed_description: OMGYES highlights three distinct orgasm pathways beyond standard clitoral climax: G-region pleasure (often needing extended warmup before it shifts from odd or queasy to deeply enjoyable), cervical/deep-end or "belly" orgasms (requiring gentle sustained internal contact rather than pounding), and dual orgasms (synchronized clitoral and internal peaks through careful timing or double-edging). First attempts at internal types often feel wrong; patience, emotional arousal, and technique matter more than force. Preferences change session to session.
stepwise_structure: 1. Set aside curiosity rather than a performance goal; orgasm type is an exploration, not a pass/fail test.
2. Build arousal with foreplay and emotional connection—not only genital touch.
3. Choose a pathway to explore: G-region mapping, deep-end sustained contact, or dual timing (often after solo or partnered practice with each type separately).
4. Use warmup and feedback; stop or switch if pain, not just unfamiliar sensation, appears.
5. Repeat across sessions; internal types often need multiple tries before technique clicks.
safety_notes: Pain, bleeding, or sharp deep internal discomfort are stop signals—not something to push through for a new orgasm type.
Cervical contact should be gentle; thumping or piston-style pounding often causes pain.
Adults in consensual contexts only; not a substitute for professional care.
